title: Occurrence ordinals can relink the wrong text after document edits
reasoning: The picker returns only an ordinal index, and insertion later rescans the current document and takes that ordinal. If the document changes between Find and Link it, adding or removing the same search text before the selected occurrence shifts indices. insertLinkedValue then succeeds against a different occurrence instead of detecting that the selected occurrence is stale.
reproduction: Find two occurrences of '100' and select occurrence 1. Before insertLinkedValue runs, insert another '100' before both original matches. Passing occurrence 1 now links the original first match, not the selected second match.
recommendation: Return a stable selection token with enough context to validate the selected occurrence at insertion time, such as document revision/hash plus run offset and surrounding text fingerprint. Refuse with null or an error if the fingerprint no longer matches.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The link tests call find/insert against unchanged bytes. They do not simulate a document edit between occurrence discovery and insertion.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that discovers occurrences in one docx, mutates the document by inserting the same search text earlier, then verifies insertion of the old selected occurrence is rejected rather than applied to a shifted match.
minimumFixScope: Update the LinkableOccurrence contract and insertLinkedValue validation in packages/core/src/links/word-links.ts, then adjust the desktop create-link payload to pass the validation token.
